verdict.rationale: SAM.gov lets users obtain API keys tied to their account and create separate System Accounts, which require approval. Data access is tiered (Public, FOUO, Sensitive) by the account's sensitivity level, giving a coarse form of privilege separation suited to a dedicated agent credential. However, scoping is set at the account and sensitivity-tier level, not as fine-grained per-key permissions. Missing for 10: per-key scope selection (e.g. specific endpoints or read-only), self-service issuance of multiple scoped keys per agent, key expiry/rotation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.
